source.title: Provable Memorization via Deep Neural Networks using Sub-linear Parameters
source.authors: Sejun Park; Jaeho Lee; Chulhee Yun; Jin-Woo Shin

record.tranche_reason: The paper studies theoretical memorization capacity and empirical depth–width trade-offs, but does not test random-label fitting, unstructured inputs, label-noise sweeps, regularization effects on random-label fitting, or learning order.
record.gate_note: The paper's arbitrary-label memorization results are theoretical existence/construction results, not experiments training standard networks with stochastic gradient methods on random labels. Its experiments train on CIFAR-10 and SVHN with their dataset labels. Cited findings are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The paper proves representational capacity for arbitrary labels through constructed weights, without establishing that stochastic gradient training finds them. Its SGD experiments use ordinary CIFAR-10 and SVHN labels. Neither result tests V1–V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors prove sublinear-parameter memorization under Δ-separateness, with depth benefits and width-three constructions. Their true-label experiments favor deeper networks for training accuracy and suggest width can improve generalization after fitting. They explicitly distinguish constructive capacity from SGD success when very narrow networks fail.
record.recipe_differences: Theoretical constructions establish that specially structured networks can memorize arbitrary labels under a Δ-separateness condition. The experiments compare residual network depth and width on CIFAR-10 and SVHN using dataset labels; they do not apply the random-label SGD recipe in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported training and test accuracy trends vary by dataset: increasing depth is associated with lower test accuracy on CIFAR-10 and higher test accuracy on SVHN. Training accuracy varies with architecture depth and width.

fits_no_version.finding: At approximately 50,000 parameters, deeper, narrower residual networks improve training accuracy; test accuracy decreases on CIFAR-10 and increases on SVHN.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Depth–width trade-offs affect fitting and generalization on true-label image datasets, with dataset-dependent test-accuracy trends.

fits_no_version.finding: The CIFAR-10 sweep includes 15-channel networks exceeding 99% training accuracy, while 5-channel networks fail to memorize.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Width affects whether SGD-trained residual networks fit true-label CIFAR-10 in the tested depth sweep.

fits_no_version.finding: Constructive theorems establish memorization of arbitrary labels on separated inputs with sublinear parameter counts, including width-three networks. Appendix C extends applicability to Gaussian inputs through a separation bound.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under separation and parameter-precision assumptions, suitably constructed deep networks can represent arbitrary finite labelings with sublinear parameter counts; SGD learnability is unresolved.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Conference on Learning Theory (COLT 2021; Proceedings of Machine Learning Research, volume 134)
record.problems: The empirical experiments use CIFAR-10 and SVHN dataset labels and do not address the claim versions' random-label or unstructured-input conditions. The text gives qualitative architecture trends for Figure 2 without per-architecture numerical values or uncertainty estimates; results are averaged over three trials.
record.rows_left_out: No reported results matching V1–V6 were found. The theoretical theorems on existence of networks capable of memorizing arbitrary labels do not train models or report experimental outcomes, so they are not rows. Figure 4's SVHN width/depth sweep is not extracted separately because the supplied text only says it uses the same setup and does not describe its results in prose; the figure-only results cannot be interpreted from the text.

untested.parts: SGD fitting of completely random labels, chance test performance, and unchanged architecture and training hyperparameters.
Relative training time for true and random labels and convergence across corruption fractions.
Training the same networks to zero error on shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit and steadily worsening test error across a label-corruption sweep.
Regularization comparisons for random-label fitting and true-label generalization after removing regularization.
Temporal ordering of learning real patterns and memorizing noisy or random labels.

record.verdict_notes: Theoretical existence of fitting weights does not establish the optimization behavior named by these versions. The use of weight decay in Appendix A supplies no regularization comparison for V5.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label training, chance test error, and unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
Training-time comparison for true versus random labels and convergence across corruption fractions.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Training and test error across fractions of randomly corrupted labels.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, or augmentation on fitting random labels and true-label generalization after their removal.
Whether real patterns are learned before noisy or random labels during training.

rows.subject: residual networks (five architectures: 29×2, 25×3, 22×4, 20×5, 19×6)
rows.operation_detail: Measured training accuracy across architectures with varying channels and residual blocks.
rows.value: As architecture becomes deeper and narrower, training accuracy increases.
rows.note: Qualitative result across the five architectures; the paper does not give textual per-architecture values. This concerns training on CIFAR-10 labels, not random labels.
rows.check: The reported training-accuracy trend concerns true CIFAR-10 labels, so it cannot establish random-label fitting.

rows.subject: residual networks (five architectures: 29×2, 25×3, 22×4, 20×5, 19×6)
rows.operation_detail: Measured test accuracy across architectures with varying channels and residual blocks.
rows.value: Test accuracy decreases as depth increases.
rows.note: Qualitative trend across the five architectures; no textual per-architecture values. Training used dataset labels.
rows.check: The test-accuracy trend concerns an architecture sweep with true labels, without label corruption.

rows.subject: residual networks (five architectures: 29×2, 25×3, 22×4, 20×5, 19×6)
rows.operation_detail: Measured test accuracy across architectures with varying channels and residual blocks.
rows.value: Test accuracy increases as depth increases.
rows.note: Qualitative trend across the five architectures; no textual per-architecture values. Training used dataset labels.
rows.check: The test-accuracy trend concerns an architecture sweep with true SVHN labels, without label corruption.

rows.subject: residual networks with 15 channels
rows.operation_detail: Measured training accuracy while varying channels and residual blocks.
rows.note: The paper describes this as successfully memorizing the CIFAR-10 dataset; this is not a random-label condition.
rows.check: Over 99% training accuracy is reported for true CIFAR-10 labels. Change observed to cannot_determine relative to these versions. The prose does not establish that every tested depth with 15 channels exceeds 99%.

rows.subject: residual networks with 5 channels
rows.operation_detail: Measured training accuracy while varying channels and residual blocks.
rows.value: too narrow networks (e.g., 5-channels) fail to memorize
rows.note: The paper does not give a numerical accuracy for this condition; it states that these networks fail to memorize the CIFAR-10 dataset.
rows.check: Failure of 5-channel networks to memorize true CIFAR-10 labels does not measure any claim version; change absent to cannot_determine.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
